source_report: World class compliance department map (verified 2026-09-26) plus its research notes
status_rule: verified = the report cites a primary source (government, regulator, official platform or vendor page) for the row and does not label it UNVERIFIED or secondary; house rules are founder-locked. Everything else is unverified. Unverified or expired rows block every gate they feed when they apply.
in_force_note: The seed takes force only when Andre approves its SHA-256 (proposal kind 'seed'). Until then every gate is blocked.

rows.title: Security standard 110% and Vanta-class control program
rows.obligation: Security is held to Andre's '110%' standard. Compliance runs a Vanta-class program: continuous control checks with SLA, audit evidence, policies, people on/off-boarding, vendor risk and a trust center. A control with no passing result inside its SLA is red.

rows.title: Clippers must be 18 or older (hard rule, no guardian path)
rows.obligation: No clipper under 18 is activated or paid. Age is established by a neutral date-of-birth field plus one highly effective age check attested by Verification and Integrity; self-declaration alone never passes.

rows.title: Gate doctrine: fail closed, cite a written rule, stale or unverified rules block
rows.obligation: Compliance is the hard gate before activation, payout and publish. Every block names an obligation id from the register. Missing facts, unreachable dependencies, and any applicable row that is expired or unverified block the gate that depends on it.

rows.title: Only Andre approves a rule into force
rows.obligation: No register row, version, or change takes effect without Andre's approval token. Intelligences draft; they never approve.

rows.title: Jurisdictions: operate
rows.obligation: Operate in the United States (US), the United Kingdom (GB) and Canada outside Quebec (CA except CA-QC). Canadian targets must be given at province level; bare 'CA' counts as including CA-QC.

rows.title: Jurisdictions: conditional (EU kit required)
rows.obligation: Germany, the Netherlands, Ireland, Spain and Italy are allowed only with the EU kit: current EU-kit version acknowledged; local ad label per country (its register row must be verified); AI-manipulation disclosure when synthetic or manipulated media is used; no EU behavioural tracking on ZBM-operated pages; for client campaigns, the MSA assigns EAA, cookie and GDPR duties for the client's own store to the client.

rows.title: Jurisdictions: refuse
rows.obligation: Refuse France (including French-language campaigns aimed at France), Quebec (CA-QC), and OFAC comprehensively sanctioned jurisdictions (Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Crimea incl. Sevastopol, and the so-called DNR/LNR regions). Any jurisdiction not on the operate or conditional list is refused by default.
rows.effective_note: Jurisdiction ruling, Sep 26, 2026; default-deny for unlisted jurisdictions is a spec choice

rows.title: No cold outbound to Canada
rows.obligation: No unsolicited email, DM, SMS or call to any person or business in Canada. Canadian creators are recruited inbound only.

rows.title: Accessibility: WCAG 2.1 AA before publish
rows.obligation: Every site, landing page, form, client portal and video ZBM/ZBC publishes passes an automated WCAG 2.1 AA check on the exact content being published (video: captions). Overlay widgets are not a remediation. Result is kept as evidence.

rows.title: Tracking disclosure, consent banner and opt-out
rows.obligation: Any site or page that uses cookies or tracking discloses the tracking, shows a consent banner and offers an opt-out before non-essential tracking runs.

rows.title: Required documents present and current
rows.obligation: Privacy policy, terms of service and required forms are present on every site, page, form and portal, at the version Legal (37) marks current. Legal drafts; Compliance enforces presence and currency.

rows.title: Money never touches Compliance
rows.obligation: Compliance rules allowed/blocked only. It holds no amounts, rates or balances and never moves money; Finance (31) pays.

rows.title: Verified view definition
rows.obligation: A payable view is a platform-reported view on the clip at a settlement date at least the configured settlement lag after posting (report: 7-14 days; default 14), after the platform's own filtering, with the anomaly screen passed, no purchased-engagement indicators, the clip still live at the end of the minimum live period, and a clawback clause for views the platform later removes. Verification and Integrity attests; Compliance checks the attestation.
rows.effective_note: Definition taken from the report; takes force only when Andre approves the seed

rows.title: Endorsement Guides: disclose material connections
rows.obligation: Every paid clip or paid endorsement discloses the material connection clearly and conspicuously (unavoidable in social media). Payment per view is a material connection. Advertiser, endorser and agency (16 CFR 255.1(d)-(f)) are each liable.
rows.penalty_note: Via FTC Act s.5; $53,088/violation only after an order or penalty-offense notice.

rows.title: Disclosure inside the video, early, audio and visual
rows.obligation: In video, the disclosure is in the video itself, not only the description; not at the end, not behind MORE, not in a hashtag cluster; audio and visual when there is voice; repeated periodically in live streams.

rows.title: Approved disclosure words
rows.obligation: Acceptable: 'advertisement', 'ad', 'sponsored', '#ad', '#sponsored'. Not acceptable: 'sp', 'spon', 'collab', standalone 'thanks'.

rows.title: Train and monitor the network; delegation does not relieve
rows.obligation: Advertisers need reasonable programs to train and monitor network members; delegating to an outside company does not relieve responsibility; pre-approval recommended. Gate: disclosure-training attestation before clipper activation; monitoring log per payout.

rows.title: No buying, selling or distributing fake views
rows.obligation: Unlawful to sell or distribute, or purchase or procure, fake indicators of social media influence ('views, plays', likes, followers) known or that should be known to be fake. Payout only on verified views (HR-13).
rows.penalty_note: $53,088 per violation (16 CFR 1.98, 2025 level frozen through 2026)

rows.title: No pay conditioned on sentiment
rows.obligation: No compensation conditioned on expressing a particular sentiment. Campaign pay basis must be reach of disclosed ads (verified views), never positive framing.
rows.penalty_note: $53,088 per violation (16 CFR 1.98, 2025 level frozen through 2026)

rows.title: No fake testimonials or misrepresented experience
rows.obligation: No testimonial that misrepresents the reviewer's existence or experience; a creator never claims personal use they do not have.
rows.penalty_note: $53,088 per violation (16 CFR 1.98, 2025 level frozen through 2026)

rows.title: No review suppression services
rows.obligation: ZBM/ZBC does not suppress reviews (threats, false accusations, sentiment-based suppression) for any client.
rows.penalty_note: $53,088 per violation (16 CFR 1.98, 2025 level frozen through 2026)

rows.title: Substantiate claims before they air; escalate health and earnings claims
rows.obligation: Every objective claim has a reasonable basis before it airs; health claims need competent and reliable scientific evidence; earnings or income claims (including ZBC recruiting copy such as 'earn $Y per 1,000 views') need typical-results substantiation. A claim file is approved per campaign before scripting.
rows.penalty_note: Injunction and redress under s.5; $53,088/violation if under order. Operation AI Comply cases ran $15.9M-$25M+.

rows.title: Business Opportunity / Earnings Claim Rule: proposals only
rows.obligation: January 2025 NPRMs are proposals, not in force. Business-opportunity or MLM clients are held for counsel review.
rows.penalty_note: 16 CFR 437 existing rule: $53,088/violation; proposals not in force.

rows.title: Impersonation Rule: no false affiliation; release for real likeness
rows.obligation: Do not pose as, or imply affiliation with, endorsement by or sponsorship from, a business or government. Any real person's likeness or voice needs a signed release on file.
rows.penalty_note: $53,088 per violation (16 CFR 1.98, 2025 level frozen through 2026)

rows.title: CAN-SPAM for every commercial email
rows.obligation: Commercial email identifies itself as an ad, has a valid postal address and a working opt-out honored within 10 business days; sender and promoted company are both liable; vendors must be monitored.

rows.title: TCPA: prior express written consent; revocation honored
rows.obligation: Autodialed or prerecorded marketing calls and texts need prior express written consent (signed, timestamped artifact per number); the one-to-one consent rule was vacated 2025-01-24; revocation by any reasonable means honored within 10 business days (from 2025-04-11).

rows.title: TCPA cross-channel revoke-all from 2027-01-31
rows.obligation: A revocation in response to one message type applies to all future robocalls/robotexts from the caller; build cross-channel revoke logic before 2027-01-31.

rows.title: COPPA: child-directed clients and channels held
rows.obligation: Amended COPPA Rule in force (effective 2025-06-23; compliance 2026-04-22). Child-directed clients, products or creator channels are blocked pending counsel; age screens are neutral.
rows.penalty_note: $53,088 per violation (16 CFR 1.98, 2025 level frozen through 2026)

rows.title: Subscriptions: ROSCA governs (Click-to-Cancel vacated)
rows.obligation: Subscription checkouts disclose material terms before consent, capture affirmative (unchecked) consent with timestamp, and offer an online cancel path as simple as sign-up. Click-to-Cancel Rule vacated July 2025; FTC ANPRM comments closed 2026-04-13.

rows.title: Health Breach Notification Rule if a health-app client shares data
rows.obligation: If a client shares consumer health data with ZBM, activation requires an HBNR service-provider clause and no pixel-based health-data sharing; otherwise not applicable.
rows.penalty_note: $53,088 per violation (16 CFR 1.98, 2025 level frozen through 2026)

rows.title: All US persons must comply; strict liability
rows.obligation: Every US person, including a one-person California company, complies with OFAC sanctions on a strict-liability basis; any entity 50%+ owned by blocked persons is blocked. Screen before onboarding and before every payout.
rows.penalty_note: IEEPA max $377,700 or 2x transaction, whichever greater (2025 level, operative for 2026).

rows.title: Screening control: SDN + Consolidated, list version, re-screen every payout
rows.obligation: Screen name, aliases, DOB and country against the SDN and Consolidated lists with fuzzy matching; store result, timestamp and list version; any potential match opens a hold for manual review; re-screen on every payout run; keep screening lists current (OFAC names failure to update screening software as a root cause).
rows.penalty_note: Program adequacy is a mitigating factor under 31 CFR 501 App. A.

rows.title: Entity payees: screen owners of 25% or more
rows.obligation: For a payee that is a company, collect and screen every owner of 25% or more (50 Percent Rule).

rows.title: Hard block comprehensively sanctioned jurisdictions
rows.obligation: Hard-block payees, creators, clients and campaign targets in Cuba, Iran, North Korea, and Crimea/DNR/LNR and other occupied regions. Syria's comprehensive program ended 2025-07-01 (now list-based, high risk).
rows.penalty_note: IEEPA max $377,700 or 2x transaction; strict liability.

rows.title: Model A only: pay creators from own funds for services to ZBC
rows.obligation: A person that accepts and transmits funds only integral to its own provision of services is not a money transmitter (31 CFR 1010.100(ff)(5)(ii)). Payout requires the Model A structure (no pooled client funds).

rows.title: Pooled client funds need a 2010(l) agent-of-payee structure
rows.obligation: If client funds are pooled and forwarded to creators (Model B), a preexisting written contract must make delivery to ZBC satisfy the client's obligation to the creator; counsel item.

rows.title: Payout rail verification does not replace ZBC's own KYC
rows.obligation: The rail must report the payee account verified and payouts enabled, and ZBC keeps its own legal name, address and country record; Stripe: 'Don't rely on Stripe's verification to meet any independent legal KYC or verification requirements.'
rows.penalty_note: No direct penalty; supports OFAC/tax obligations.

rows.title: No payout without W-9 (TIN-matched) or W-8BEN; 24% backup withholding
rows.obligation: Backup withholding is 24% when no correct TIN; begin within 30 business days of a CP2100; first B notice within 15 business days. Rule: no payout until a TIN-matched W-9 or a W-8BEN/W-8BEN-E is on file (Finance 31 attests).
rows.penalty_note: Withholding liability plus information-return penalties (amounts not verified).

rows.title: TIN Matching before first reportable payout
rows.obligation: Validate name/TIN through IRS TIN Matching (e-Services) and store the result for US payees.

rows.title: 1099-NEC threshold $2,000 for 2026 payments (indexed from 2027)
rows.obligation: Finance tracks YTD payments per payee and files 1099-NEC at $2,000 for payments made in 2026. Not a payout precondition: the W-9/W-8 rule (US-IRS-BWH) applies from the first dollar.
rows.effective_note: Payments after 2025-12-31; Pub. L. 119-21 section numbers UNVERIFIED on primary

rows.title: 1099-K threshold $20,000 and 200 transactions
rows.obligation: Form 1099-K reporting only when gross payments exceed $20,000 and transactions exceed 200; Finance tracks rail configuration.

rows.title: Foreign creators: W-8BEN plus services-outside-US attestation
rows.obligation: Personal-service income is sourced where services are performed; a creator working abroad needs a W-8BEN and an attestation that services are performed outside the US; any US-performed portion is 30% or treaty rate.

rows.title: W-8BEN validity period
rows.obligation: W-8BEN is valid through the third calendar year after signing (standard rule, not verified); expired forms block payout.

rows.title: Rights cleared; no copyright strike on the posting account
rows.obligation: Platforms terminate repeat infringers (17 U.S.C. 512(i)(1)(A)); a paid clip needs footage covered by a written sublicense (client -> ZBC -> clipper) and no copyright strike or removal on the account at settlement.

rows.title: YouTube: paid promotion checkbox
rows.obligation: Paid promotions are declared with YouTube's paid promotion setting in video details; creator and partners are responsible for legal compliance.
rows.penalty_note: Platform enforcement; FTC exposure if undisclosed.

rows.title: YouTube: fake engagement policy
rows.obligation: No third-party services that artificially inflate views; artificial views are removed; warning -> strikes -> termination (3 strikes in 90 days).

rows.title: TikTok: commercial content disclosure toggle
rows.obligation: Branded content (promotion for payment or any other incentive) must enable the commercial content disclosure toggle; the promoted product must be clear without visiting the profile.
rows.penalty_note: Content removal; FTC exposure if undisclosed.

rows.title: TikTok: branded-content prohibited industries
rows.obligation: No branded content for adult, alcohol, tobacco, drugs, gambling and financial schemes, pharmaceuticals and weight loss, political, weapons, counterfeit categories.

rows.title: TikTok: no artificial engagement, no bulk accounts
rows.obligation: No trade in artificial engagement; no accounts operated in bulk, by unauthorized automation, or to distribute high-volume commercial content. Clippers disclose every account used.
rows.penalty_note: Account bans; loss of paid clips.

rows.title: TikTok: Commercial Music Library for commercial content
rows.obligation: Paid clips on TikTok use the Commercial Music Library, a licensed track, or no music; businesses cannot use the general library commercially. Track id declared.

rows.title: X: Paid Partnership disclosure on
rows.obligation: Posts that are part of a paid partnership published as organic posts must have the 'Paid Partnership' disclosure on.

rows.title: X: paid-partnership prohibited categories
rows.obligation: No paid partnerships for adult, alcohol, contraceptives, dating, drugs, political/social issues for commercial purposes, supplements, pharmaceuticals, tobacco/vaping, weapons, weight loss; AU/EU/UK limits on financial products, crypto, gambling.

rows.title: Snapchat: paid partnership tool
rows.obligation: Content you were incentivized to post (money or free gifts) is labelled with Snap's paid partnership tool; disclosures visible and appropriate.

rows.title: Meta (Instagram/Facebook): branded content label and inauthentic behavior
rows.obligation: Meta's branded content policy (paid partnership label) and inauthentic-behavior policy could not be read from primary sources. Do not quote. Blocks Meta clips until verified.

rows.title: Twitch: sponsorship disclosure
rows.obligation: Whether Twitch imposes a mandatory disclosure label is UNVERIFIED (safety-center page 404). Blocks Twitch until verified.

rows.title: Age assurance: neutral DOB plus one highly effective method
rows.obligation: Self-declaration is not highly effective. Accepted methods: open banking, photo-ID matching, facial age estimation, mobile-operator check, credit-card check, digital identity service, email-based estimation. The DOB field is neutral (no default, no pre-checked 18+ box). Result stored as pass/fail with vendor, method, timestamp; no ID number stored.
rows.penalty_note: Supports HR-02; COPPA $53,088/violation if a child is onboarded.

rows.title: New York GBL 396-b: disclose synthetic performers in ads
rows.obligation: Anyone who produces or creates an ad conspicuously discloses a synthetic performer when it has actual knowledge. Applies to any ad seen in New York.

rows.title: Tennessee ELVIS Act: consent for real voice or likeness
rows.obligation: No commercial use of an identifiable person's voice or AI voice replica without written consent.
rows.penalty_note: Civil and criminal; treble damages for knowing use.

rows.title: Utah AI Policy Act: GenAI disclosure for consumer chatbots
rows.obligation: Disclose GenAI use on request and proactively in high-risk conversational interactions; sunsets July 2027.

rows.title: Political-deepfake laws (28 states): no political or candidate ads without counsel
rows.obligation: 28 states regulate deepfakes in political communications; no political or candidate advertising without counsel review.

rows.title: Colorado SB 26-189 and Texas TRAIGA: monitor
rows.obligation: Colorado SB 26-189 (effective 2027-01-01) targets consequential decisions; Texas TRAIGA (effective 2026-01-01) has intent-based prohibitions and no private-sector disclosure duty. Monitor; no ad-creative gate.

rows.title: CalOPPA: conspicuous privacy policy
rows.obligation: Any commercial site collecting PII from Californians posts a conspicuous privacy policy (details UNVERIFIED; statute not fetched).

rows.title: Delete Act: no audience-data sale without data-broker analysis
rows.obligation: A business selling data about consumers it has no direct relationship with registers as a data broker and processes DROP deletions (live 2026-08-01, 45-day login cadence).

rows.title: California AB 2013 / SB 942 applicability
rows.obligation: AB 2013 (2026-01-01) reaches ZBM only if it publishes or substantially modifies a GenAI model; SB 942 (operative 2026-08-02) only providers with over 1M monthly users. Annual applicability check.

rows.title: Age-Appropriate Design Code: partially revived
rows.obligation: Ninth Circuit (2026-03-12) revived age estimation and default-high-privacy provisions; readings conflict on dark patterns. Consumer client sites likely accessed by children are held until the opinion is read.

rows.title: State mini-TCPA laws (FL, OK, MD, WA, TX, AZ): universal SMS profile
rows.obligation: Marketing texts/calls: signed timestamped written consent; recipient-local 8am-8pm (FL allows to 9pm); at most 3 messages per 24 hours on one subject (OK, MD); immediate opt-out; Texas registration unless consent-based.
rows.penalty_note: FL/OK $500-$1,500 per message; WA greater of actual or $1,000; private actions.

rows.title: CCPA/CPRA comprehensive privacy law: threshold counter
rows.obligation: Applies once ZBM crosses: $25M revenue OR 100k consumers OR 50%+ revenue from selling/sharing. Universal opt-out (GPC) required: Yes. Cure period: None. Keep a per-state consumer counter; below threshold, no gate.

rows.title: VCDPA comprehensive privacy law: threshold counter
rows.obligation: Applies once ZBM crosses: 100k, or 25k + 50%. Universal opt-out (GPC) required: No. Cure period: 30 days. Keep a per-state consumer counter; below threshold, no gate.

rows.title: CPA comprehensive privacy law: threshold counter
rows.obligation: Applies once ZBM crosses: 100k, or 25k + revenue from sales. Universal opt-out (GPC) required: Yes. Cure period: None. Keep a per-state consumer counter; below threshold, no gate.

rows.title: CTDPA comprehensive privacy law: threshold counter
rows.obligation: Applies once ZBM crosses: 35k (lowered 2026-07-01), or 25k + 25%; notice must disclose LLM-training use. Universal opt-out (GPC) required: Yes. Cure period: None. Keep a per-state consumer counter; below threshold, no gate.

rows.title: UCPA comprehensive privacy law: threshold counter
rows.obligation: Applies once ZBM crosses: $25M revenue AND (100k or 25k + 50%). Universal opt-out (GPC) required: No. Cure period: 30 days. Keep a per-state consumer counter; below threshold, no gate.

rows.title: TDPSA comprehensive privacy law: threshold counter
rows.obligation: Applies once ZBM crosses: No numeric threshold; SBA small-business exemption except sensitive-data consent (nuance UNVERIFIED). Universal opt-out (GPC) required: Yes. Cure period: 30 days. Keep a per-state consumer counter; below threshold, no gate.

rows.title: OCPA comprehensive privacy law: threshold counter
rows.obligation: Applies once ZBM crosses: 100k, or 25k + 25%. Universal opt-out (GPC) required: Yes. Cure period: None. Keep a per-state consumer counter; below threshold, no gate.

rows.title: MCDPA comprehensive privacy law: threshold counter
rows.obligation: Applies once ZBM crosses: 25k, or 15k + 25%. Universal opt-out (GPC) required: Yes. Cure period: None. Keep a per-state consumer counter; below threshold, no gate.

rows.title: FDBR comprehensive privacy law: threshold counter
rows.obligation: Applies once ZBM crosses: $1B global revenue AND platform/ad conditions. Universal opt-out (GPC) required: No. Cure period: 45 days. Keep a per-state consumer counter; below threshold, no gate.

rows.title: DPDPA comprehensive privacy law: threshold counter
rows.obligation: Applies once ZBM crosses: 35k, or 10k + 20%. Universal opt-out (GPC) required: Yes. Cure period: None. Keep a per-state consumer counter; below threshold, no gate.

rows.title: ICDPA comprehensive privacy law: threshold counter
rows.obligation: Applies once ZBM crosses: 100k, or 25k + 50%. Universal opt-out (GPC) required: No. Cure period: 90 days. Keep a per-state consumer counter; below threshold, no gate.

rows.title: NDPA comprehensive privacy law: threshold counter
rows.obligation: Applies once ZBM crosses: No numeric threshold; SBA small-business exemption. Universal opt-out (GPC) required: Yes. Cure period: 30 days. Keep a per-state consumer counter; below threshold, no gate.

rows.title: NHPA comprehensive privacy law: threshold counter
rows.obligation: Applies once ZBM crosses: 35k, or 10k + 25%. Universal opt-out (GPC) required: Yes. Cure period: None. Keep a per-state consumer counter; below threshold, no gate.

rows.title: NJDPA comprehensive privacy law: threshold counter
rows.obligation: Applies once ZBM crosses: 100k, or 25k + 50%. Universal opt-out (GPC) required: Yes. Cure period: None. Keep a per-state consumer counter; below threshold, no gate.

rows.title: TIPA comprehensive privacy law: threshold counter
rows.obligation: Applies once ZBM crosses: $25M revenue AND (175k or 25k + 50%). Universal opt-out (GPC) required: No. Cure period: 60 days. Keep a per-state consumer counter; below threshold, no gate.

rows.title: MCDPA comprehensive privacy law: threshold counter
rows.obligation: Applies once ZBM crosses: 100k, or 25k + 25%. Universal opt-out (GPC) required: Yes. Cure period: None. Keep a per-state consumer counter; below threshold, no gate.

rows.title: MODPA comprehensive privacy law: threshold counter
rows.obligation: Applies once ZBM crosses: 35k, or 10k + 20%. Universal opt-out (GPC) required: Yes. Cure period: 60 days. Keep a per-state consumer counter; below threshold, no gate.

rows.title: INCDPA comprehensive privacy law: threshold counter
rows.obligation: Applies once ZBM crosses: 100k, or 25k + 50%. Universal opt-out (GPC) required: No. Cure period: 30 days per tracker; another source says removed (CQ-09). Keep a per-state consumer counter; below threshold, no gate.

rows.title: KCDPA comprehensive privacy law: threshold counter
rows.obligation: Applies once ZBM crosses: 100k, or 25k + 50%. Universal opt-out (GPC) required: No. Cure period: 30 days per tracker; another source says removed (CQ-09). Keep a per-state consumer counter; below threshold, no gate.

rows.title: RIDTPPA comprehensive privacy law: threshold counter
rows.obligation: Applies once ZBM crosses: 35k, or 10k + 20%. Universal opt-out (GPC) required: No. Cure period: None. Keep a per-state consumer counter; below threshold, no gate.

rows.title: Enacted, not yet effective: LA, OK, AL, VT
rows.obligation: Louisiana and Oklahoma 2027-01-01; Alabama 2027-05-01; Vermont 2028-01-01. Add counters before each date.

rows.title: Honor Global Privacy Control on agency-run sites
rows.obligation: Twelve states require recognition of universal opt-out signals (CA, CO, CT, DE, MD, MN, MT, NE, NH, NJ, OR, TX). Report: honor GPC on every agency-operated site now.
rows.penalty_note: CA $7,988/violation; Healthline paid $1.55M for ignoring GPC.

rows.title: CPPA 2025 regulations (risk assessments, cyber audits, ADMT)
rows.obligation: Risk assessments from 2026-01-01; ADMT 2027-01-01; attestations and certifications 2028-2030. Applies only to CCPA businesses; clients may flow expectations down.

rows.title: GDPR reach and Art. 27 representative
rows.obligation: GDPR applies to a non-EU company offering services to or monitoring people in the EU; an Art. 27 representative is required unless processing is occasional and low risk (counsel item CQ-05). Keep EU creator data minimal; no EU behavioural tracking on ZBM pages.

rows.title: EU AI Act Art. 50(4): disclose AI-generated or manipulated media
rows.obligation: Deployers who generate or manipulate a real person's image, audio or video disclose it; reaches third-country deployers whose output is used in the EU; applicable 2026-08-02, not postponed by the Digital Omnibus.
rows.penalty_note: Up to EUR 15M or 3% of turnover.

rows.title: European Accessibility Act for consumer e-commerce
rows.obligation: Applies from 2025-06-28 to any provider offering e-commerce services to EU consumers; microenterprise exemption wording UNVERIFIED. Client storefronts targeting EU need it.

rows.title: France influencer law: refuse until counsel
rows.obligation: Non-EU influencers targeting France need an EU legal representative and civil-liability insurance; written contracts; labels 'publicité' or 'collaboration commerciale' for the whole promotion; active DGCCRF unit. France is refused (HR-07).
rows.penalty_note: Criminal referral; EUR 300,000 / 2 years (UNVERIFIED on primary).

rows.title: Italy AGCOM: immediately visible ad label
rows.obligation: Commercial content intended for users in Italy carries an immediately visible label ('Pubblicità', 'ADV', 'Sponsorizzato'); hashtags or brand tags alone are insufficient. Registration only at 500k followers or 1M average monthly views.
rows.penalty_note: Warnings and proportionate fines (amounts not stated).

rows.title: Spain RD 444/2024: special-relevance creator registration
rows.obligation: Creators with 300,000 EUR+ platform income and 1M followers on one platform (or 2M aggregate) and 24+ videos a year must register. Spanish creators attest they are below the threshold or are held.

rows.title: Spain: local ad label ('Publicidad')
rows.obligation: Label text 'Publicidad' comes from the report's EU kit; no Spanish primary source was cited.

rows.title: Germany UWG 5a: label commercial purpose ('Werbung'/'Anzeige')
rows.obligation: Failing to identify a commercial purpose is misleading; enforced privately (competitor cease-and-desist). Statute not fetched.

rows.title: Netherlands: CvdM supervision and label ('Reclame'/'Advertentie')
rows.obligation: CvdM supervises all video uploaders since 2025-06-16 (registration only at 100k followers); ad labelling required; label text source (Reclame Code) not fetched.
rows.penalty_note: One fine of EUR 6,075 by mid-2025.

rows.title: Ireland: ad label rule
rows.obligation: The report names Ireland as conditional but cites no Irish rule or label. Unverified until sourced.

rows.title: UK hidden advertising: rules apply across the supply chain
rows.obligation: Ads must be obviously identifiable (CAP Code); undisclosed paid editorial (DMCC Banned Practice 12) and fake or concealed incentivised reviews (BP13) are banned; liability runs to creators, brands, platforms and agencies. Paid clips that look like organic fan content are BP12.
rows.penalty_note: CMA fines up to 10% of global turnover since 2025-04-06 (secondary).

rows.title: CASL: consent for any commercial message accessed in Canada
rows.obligation: A commercial electronic message accessed from a computer in Canada needs consent, identification and an unsubscribe, wherever the sender is. Statute not fetched.
rows.penalty_note: AMPs up to CAD 10M per violation (organizations).

rows.title: Competition Bureau: disclose all material connections
rows.obligation: Influencers disclose all material connections prominently, on each platform, without clicking to expand; the Act applies to anyone promoting a product or business interest.

rows.title: Quebec Law 25: refuse until counsel
rows.obligation: Applies with no threshold to anyone carrying on an enterprise in Quebec; opt-in consent before identifying trackers; private right of action. Quebec is refused (HR-07).
rows.penalty_note: Penal fines to CAD 25M or 4% of worldwide turnover.

rows.title: Program design: DOJ ECCP, ISO 37301 4.5/4.6, NIST GV.OC-03
rows.obligation: Maintain an obligation register with dated reviews and evidence; identify new and changed obligations; data access to test controls; human baseline over AI decisions and fast correction of AI errors.
rows.penalty_note: Program adequacy affects charging and penalties.

rows.title: Are ZBC's clippers independent contractors under California AB 5's ABC test, and does any AB 2257 creative exemption fit?
